r=⟨2\operatorname{cot}⁡(2\pi t),\,{sin}^{2}⁡(2\pi t)⟩,\,0<t<\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Calculate the components of the velocity vector $v$ at time $t=\frac{1}{8}.$ Do not round the answers.

feedback.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v$ at time $t=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,1+\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we substitute into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-(\frac{\pi }{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0-(\frac{\pi }{2})(1),1+(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{\pi }{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$
